articles.title: Former UN rights chief awarded Nobel Peace Prize
articles.summary: Former UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Navi Pillay was on Friday announced as the winner of the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize.
articles.content:
The South African jurist was honoured “for her efforts to promote peace and international law”, the Norwegian Nobel Committee said in a statement.

The committee said it presented the award “to a person who with exceptional courage and integrity has led the way towards a more comprehensive global legal order,” noting that she “has been instrumental in ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide are prosecuted.”

A lifelong champion of human rights

Ms. Pillay served as the UN human rights chief from September 2008 through August 2014, but her career has spanned more than 50 years - from fighting apartheid in her homeland to defending civilians in conflict zones.

She is a former chair of the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory and was appointed a judge on the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda (ICTR) and at the International Criminal Court (ICC) in the Hague.

Navanethem “Navi” PIllay was born in South Africa to a Tamil Indian family and was the first non-white woman to establish a legal practice in the country.

Tweet URL

As a lawyer, she acted as a defense attorney for anti-apartheid activists, exposing torture, and helping to establish key rights for prisoners on notorious Robben Island.

“A common thread runs from her early work defending Nelson Mandela and others who stood up against apartheid to her service as a judge in some of the key international court cases of our time,” the Nobel Committee said.

Human rights reaffirmed: Türk

On receiving the news of Ms. Pillay's win, the current UN human rights chief, Volker Türk, warmly congratulated the woman he described as a big sister.

“To say it is well deserved is a total understatement, and especially at a time when human rights are under attack on so many fronts, including from those who wield enormous power, this award is particularly poignant,” he said, speaking in Geneva.

“It is an award to all those who around the world dedicate their lives to the defense of human rights, often at great risk to their security.”

He described it as “a recognition, a reaffirmation, that human rights, the rule of law and justice and accountability are fundamental to everything - to peace, to security and prosperity.

Ms. Pillay reflected on her lifetime of fighting for human rights, justice and equality in a 2025 interview with UN News,

“I didn't think apartheid would end in my lifetime,” she recalled. “So, what happened? We had the collective support of people all over the world, even children. If we can achieve that, we can have a better human rights protection system.”

Her experience in the anti-apartheid struggle shaped her belief in international solidarity, which she carried into her role as a judge at the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda (ICTR) where she helped establish groundbreaking legal precedents in the fight against genocide and gender-based violence.

As UN human rights chief, she continued to champion the participation of civil society and victims’ voices in shaping global human rights standards.

“When the UN started, it was just a club for the States,” she told UN News. “Everything we have today for human rights protection didn’t happen just because the States woke up one day. It comes from the pressure of civil society. That’s why I value these institutions.”

articles.personality_title: Navi Pillay wins Nobel Peace Prize for decades of human rights work
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Navi Pillay is a South African lawyer and judge who has spent over 50 years fighting for human rights. She worked against apartheid in South Africa and later helped bring justice in international courts for war crimes and genocide.

**What happened** – On Friday, the Norwegian Nobel Committee announced that Navi Pillay won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize. They honored her for her courage and leadership in promoting peace and international law. She served as the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights from 2008 to 2014 and held important roles in courts dealing with crimes against humanity.

**Impact** – Pillay’s work has helped make sure people responsible for serious crimes like genocide are held accountable. She also helped improve global laws to protect human rights and gave a voice to victims around the world. Her achievements show how one person’s dedication can influence justice and peace globally.

**What's next step** – Pillay’s award highlights the ongoing need to protect human rights everywhere. It encourages governments, courts, and civil society groups to continue working together to uphold justice and prevent abuses. Her example may inspire new leaders to follow her path.

**One-sentence takeaway** – Navi Pillay’s Nobel Peace Prize honors her lifelong fight for justice and human rights, showing the power of law to promote peace worldwide.
articles.personality_title_fr: Navi Pillay reçoit le prix Nobel de la paix pour des décennies de défense des droits humains
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Navi Pillay est une avocate et juge sud-africaine qui lutte depuis plus de 50 ans pour les droits humains. Elle a combattu l’apartheid en Afrique du Sud et a ensuite aidé à rendre la justice dans des tribunaux internationaux pour crimes de guerre et génocide.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Vendredi, le Comité Nobel norvégien a annoncé que Navi Pillay recevait le prix Nobel de la paix 2026. Ils l’ont honorée pour son courage et son leadership dans la promotion de la paix et du droit international. Elle a été Haut-Commissaire des Nations Unies aux droits de l’homme de 2008 à 2014 et a occupé des postes importants dans des tribunaux traitant des crimes contre l’humanité.

**Impact** – Le travail de Pillay a aidé à garantir que les responsables de crimes graves comme le génocide soient tenus responsables. Elle a aussi contribué à améliorer les lois mondiales pour protéger les droits humains et a donné une voix aux victimes dans le monde entier. Ses réalisations montrent comment la détermination d’une personne peut influencer la justice et la paix à l’échelle mondiale.

**Prochaine étape** – Ce prix met en lumière la nécessité continue de protéger les droits humains partout. Il encourage les gouvernements, les tribunaux et la société civile à poursuivre leur travail pour défendre la justice et prévenir les abus. Son exemple peut inspirer de nouveaux leaders.

**Résumé en une phrase** – Le prix Nobel de la paix de Navi Pillay récompense son combat de toute une vie pour la justice et les droits humains, montrant le pouvoir du droit pour promouvoir la paix dans le monde.
articles.personality_title_es: Navi Pillay gana el Premio Nobel de la Paz por décadas de trabajo en derechos humanos
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Navi Pillay es una abogada y jueza sudafricana que ha dedicado más de 50 años a defender los derechos humanos. Luchó contra el apartheid en Sudáfrica y luego ayudó a llevar justicia en tribunales internacionales por crímenes de guerra y genocidio.

**Qué pasó** – El viernes, el Comité Nobel de Noruega anunció que Navi Pillay ganó el Premio Nobel de la Paz 2026. La reconocieron por su valentía y liderazgo para promover la paz y el derecho internacional. Fue Alta Comisionada de la ONU para los Derechos Humanos entre 2008 y 2014 y tuvo cargos importantes en tribunales que juzgan crímenes contra la humanidad.

**Impacto** – El trabajo de Pillay ha ayudado a asegurar que los responsables de crímenes graves como el genocidio sean llevados ante la justicia. También contribuyó a mejorar las leyes globales para proteger los derechos humanos y dio voz a las víctimas en todo el mundo. Su ejemplo muestra cómo una persona puede influir en la justicia y la paz mundial.

**Próximo paso** – Este premio destaca la necesidad de seguir protegiendo los derechos humanos en todas partes. Anima a gobiernos, tribunales y grupos sociales a continuar trabajando juntos para defender la justicia y evitar abusos. Su ejemplo puede inspirar a nuevos líderes.

**Resumen en una frase** – El Premio Nobel de la Paz a Navi Pillay reconoce su lucha de toda la vida por la justicia y los derechos humanos, demostrando el poder del derecho para promover la paz en el mundo.
